186: Writing: commits, READMEs and bug reports
188: Write commit messages, READMEs and bug reports in professional English, like the ones in big projects.
190: The first line is short (roughly under 50 characters) and starts with an imperative verb, with no period at the end — as if completing the sentence “If applied, this commit will …”.
191: A prefix that says the type of change: feat (new feature), fix (bug fix), docs (documentation), refactor (restructuring), chore (maintenance), test (tests).
193: Title, a line saying what the project does, Features, Installation, Usage, Configuration, Contributing and License.
195: Summary, Steps to reproduce, Expected behavior, Actual behavior, Environment (OS and version), and Screenshots or Logs.
197: Present simple for facts (The app sends…). Past simple for what happened (I clicked…, It crashed…). Present perfect for what happened and still matters (I have tried…, It has stopped working).
199: One sentence = one idea. Cut very, really and kind of. Use the simple word instead of the fancy one (use instead of utilize).
